summary: The starter prompt clearly specifies the core goal (a Python/Beanie pipeline that extracts themes/sentiment/quote, embeds text, writes enriched documents, and provides aggregation queries). Run-environment details in the supplied skill_md fill important infra facts (existing M30 cluster, database name, DOCUMENTDB_URI env var). Several implementation details (Python version, exact models, index dimensions, app surface, tests, README, seed-data shape) are left unspecified and will be chosen by the builder unless the author clarifies them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python pipeline using Beanie ODM that reads survey response documents from DocumentDB, uses prompt engineering to extract themes, sentiment, and a representative quote from each response, embeds the text, and writes the enriched document back. Build aggregation queries that surface the top themes and sentiment distribution per survey question."
rubric.note: Core business goal and demonstration are explicit.

rubric.found_in_prompt: No explicit mention of agent workflow/framework; only "Using the DocumentDB skill"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat this as a single-agent/no-agent sample: a standalone Python pipeline (scripts + optional small API) run locally, not a multi-agent orchestration.
rubric.note: The prompt name references a skill but does not require an agent framework; this does not block starting the work.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Python pipeline" (Beanie ODM) but no explicit version
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a modern Python 3.11 (or 3.10) virtualenv; rely on pip/venv as in skill_md.
rubric.note: skill_md says python and pip resolve to a venv on the developer machine but gives no exact Python version.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Beanie ODM" (implies async driver) but no driver/version pinned
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will pick Beanie compatible versions (e.g., Beanie latest stable that supports PyMongo async / Motor), and include compatible PyMongo/Motor versions in requirements.txt with pins.
rubric.note: documentdb-driver gives singleton client and best-practice guidance but does not choose exact driver versions. Also note a potential conflict: documentdb-connection recommends PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient over Motor for new async Python code; Beanie historically uses Motor — see contradictions.

The supplied skill_md run environment explicitly states a reachable vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol) and the database name sample_customer_360_17; use that cluster. This was provided in the skill_md section of the sample.
skill_md instructs the connection string is in DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable and must not be written into files; .env.example with placeholders should be used. That covers where secrets live.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Beanie ODM" and "survey response documents" but no schema provided
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create a Beanie Document model with fields such as: _id, survey_id, question_id, respondent_id, response_text, created_at, themes (array of strings with counts/weights optional), sentiment {label,score}, representative_quote, embedding (vector), schemaVersion.
rubric.note: Data-modeling skill can guide choices (embed vs ref, schemaVersion) but the exact shape must be decided by the implementer.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include a small idempotent seed script producing a few dozen to a few hundred example survey responses in JSON, or generate synthetic examples; include a script/fixture under seeds/ and document how to run it.
rubric.note: Prompt does not say where sample data comes from or its size/licence. local-deployment skill explains seed-script patterns but does not supply the actual dataset.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Build aggregation queries that surface the top themes and sentiment distribution per survey question." No index shapes or vector index parameters specified.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create a vector index (e.g., vector-diskann for M30) with dimensions matching the chosen embedding model (or make the dimension configurable via env), and add supporting indexes (e.g., question_id, themes array as multikey). Specific index parameters (lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree) will be chosen per documentdb-vector-search guidance and recorded in README.
rubric.note: documentdb-indexing and documentdb-vector-search cover index selection and shapes; the prompt does not set exact parameters or dimensions so the implementer will choose and document them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "uses prompt engineering to extract themes, sentiment, and a representative quote... embeds the text" and "e.g. OpenAI"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use a hosted LLM + embedding provider (commonly OpenAI), with API key read from environment variables (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY). The specific chat and embedding models (e.g., gpt-4o-mini / text-embedding-3-small) will be chosen and made configurable via env.
rubric.note: Prompt requires LLM prompt-engineering and an embedding call but does not specify provider or exact models/dimensions; those choices affect index dims and cost and should be documented.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python pipeline" but no explicit surface (CLI/API/web UI)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will produce a set of CLI scripts (seed, enrich, run-aggregations) and a small sample script or minimal FastAPI endpoint to run aggregation queries for demonstration. The emphasis will be on runnable scripts rather than a full UI.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't require a web UI; a pipeline/script + sample outputs is sufficient for a gallery sample unless the author requests an API or UI.

skill_md explicitly states a ready cluster is reachable and that the sample should verify against that live cluster; do not provision another cluster. The build should create collections/indexes on that database, not deploy cloud infra.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include README commands: pip install -r requirements.txt, cp .env.example .env and fill in keys, python seeds/seed.py, python enrich/enrich.py, python aggregates/show_aggregates.py. Unit tests may be included that mock DB and AI calls.
rubric.note: Prompt asks for build but doesn't list run/test commands; skill_md expects verification against live cluster and to record what ran.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat 'done' as: seed script loads sample data idempotently; enrich pipeline updates each document with themes, sentiment, representative_quote and embedding; vector index created; aggregation queries return top themes per question and sentiment distribution; README documents steps and example outputs.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria in the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will avoid provisioning new cloud infra and will keep sample data small to limit costs; will document that large-scale tuning is out of scope.
rubric.note: No cost or compliance constraints provided; skill_md forbids creating a new cluster during runs unless allowed.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Using the DocumentDB skill" and skill_md says use .env.example and not to write connection strings
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use a conventional layout (src/, seeds/, tests/, README.md), include .env.example, pinned requirements.txt, and a README with sections: Overview, Prereqs, Setup, Run, Clean-up. Tests will use mocks or a test fixture and may not require a live cluster.
rubric.note: Some conventions (use .env.example) are mentioned in skill_md; others (pinning requirements, test patterns) are not fully specified by the prompt.

contradictions: documentdb-connection guidance recommends using PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient (and not Motor) for new async Python code, but the starter prompt mandates Beanie ODM. Beanie depends historically on Motor (an async driver). This creates a potential conflict the builder must resolve (choose Beanie-compatible driver versions, or adapt Beanie to use PyMongo Async if supported).
questions_for_author: Which LLM and embedding provider/models should the sample use (e.g., OpenAI chat + text-embedding-3-small)? This determines embedding dimensions and index shape.
Should the sample expose a CLI-only pipeline, or also include a minimal HTTP API/web UI for running the aggregations?
Which Python version should be targeted (3.10, 3.11)?
Do you require infrastructure-as-code for the cluster (Bicep/Terraform) to be included, or should the sample rely solely on the provided live cluster?
requirements_at_risk: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository. — Risk: While skill_md instructs DOCUMENTDB_URI, the prompt does not require AI model API keys or exact env var names; the builder will likely add them but it's not specified.

A `.env.example` lists every setting with placeholder values. — Risk: skill_md suggests using .env.example but the prompt doesn't demand it; implementer may or may not include all required placeholders.
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output. — Risk: prompt omits the embedding model; unless the builder documents and wires the embedding dims configurable, mismatch is possible.

The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one. — Risk: prompt asks for embeddings/indexing but does not require documenting parameter choices or how to scale.

One database client is created and reused across requests. — Risk: documentdb-driver skill covers singleton client pattern, but the prompt doesn't mandate it; builder likely to follow best practices but not guaranteed.

A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data. — Risk: prompt asks to read and enrich documents but doesn't specify an idempotent seed script; implementer may or may not include idempotency.

/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails. — Risk: prompt doesn't request endpoints or error handling specifics; implementer may not implement such defensive behavior.
Search results include the similarity score. — Risk: prompt requires embedding + aggregates but doesn't require search endpoints to surface similarity scores.
Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt`. — Risk: prompt does not mention pinning; typical builders will pin but it's not enforced.
Unit tests run without a live cluster. — Risk: prompt does not demand tests or mocking strategy; author may expect tests but none are specified.

Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type. — Risk: skill_md says a cluster already exists and forbids provisioning; reference requirement asks for IaC which the prompt did not request.

The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up. — Risk: prompt does not explicitly require a README with all those sections though skill_md expects build verification to be recorded.

The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name. — Risk: prompt doesn't mandate naming conventions; implementer may inadvertently use other product names.
